properties.name: triggers
properties.title: Triggers
properties.description: One row for each push button wired between a GPIO pin (BCM number) and ground, and what pressing it does: play, stop, toggle (stop while playing, else play), next (the next page of the playlist), run a task (a Priority Update task, set up on the row, that shows for its minutes) or play a playlist (the playlist layer goes to its first track and carries on from there). Play, stop, toggle and next can each be on one button only. A button's Long Press, held a second and let go, can do another of these actions (not a task). Not a pin the panel uses (the list says which). Changes apply within a few seconds.

properties.name: pin
properties.title: GPIO Pin
properties.description: The GPIO number (BCM) the button is wired to: the choices follow the display type chosen in Display, and the pins the panel uses are not available.

properties.name: action
properties.title: Action
properties.description: What pressing the button does. A task shows a Priority Update (its settings are set on the row) for its minutes. Play playlist starts the playlist you choose from its first track.

properties.name: playlist
properties.title: Playlist
properties.description: The playlist the button starts: it begins at its first track and carries on from there, through the playlists after it.

properties.name: longAction
properties.title: Long Press
properties.description: What holding the button for a second does, when it is let go (the Held cue says when): the same actions as a press, but not a task (the row's task is the press's). Empty: a long press does nothing.

properties.name: longPlaylist
properties.title: Long Press Playlist
properties.description: The playlist a long press starts: it begins at its first track and carries on from there.

properties.name: outputs
properties.title: Outputs
properties.description: One row for each thing the device can say something with: a GPIO output (an LED wired from a pin through a resistor to ground, or an active buzzer; the Inky Impression has an LED on pin 13, at the top centre edge of the board), a haptic motor (a DRV2605 driver on the I²C bus, such as on the Impression's Qw/ST socket) or a sound card (a USB sound stick, the Pi's headphone jack or its HDMI). A GPIO output with no pin is not connected. Feedback, below, says what each one says and when, a section for each kind. An output whose hardware is not found is said in Activity, and the others still work.

properties.name: name
properties.title: Name
properties.description: What the output is called in its kind's Feedback and in Buttons, live: LED, Buzzer, Speaker.

properties.name: kind
properties.title: Kind
properties.description: GPIO: an LED or a buzzer on a pin. Haptic: a vibration motor (felt only while touching the device, so for the buttons). Audio: a sound card.

properties.name: pin
properties.title: Pin
properties.description: The GPIO number (BCM) it is wired to. Empty: not connected. Not a pin the panel, a button or another output uses.

properties.name: speed
properties.title: Speed
properties.description: How long one blink takes, on and off: every cue speeds up or slows down with it, keeping its rhythm. Slower is easier to see from across a room. Test plays three blinks at the speed chosen now, on the saved output.

properties.name: volume
properties.title: Volume
properties.description: How loud the sound card plays the cues.

properties.name: card
properties.title: Card
properties.description: Where the sound goes. USB: the first USB sound stick or USB speaker plugged in. Headphone jack: the Pi's own (a Pi 3 B+ or 4; a Pi 5 or a Zero has none), to any powered speaker. HDMI: a display that plays sound, a receiver, or an HDMI audio extractor (one with EDID emulation works with no display); it plays only while one is connected and on.

properties.name: gpioFeedback
properties.title: GPIO Feedback
properties.description: What the GPIO outputs say, and when: one row for each event and output. Press and Long Press play once, when the button is let go; Held plays once a button has been held for a second (the cue that letting go is a long press); Problem while every track of the playlist has failed or the device waits to be set up; Drawing while the panel refreshes. One cue plays at a time on an output: a press plays over the others, Held comes before Problem, and Problem before Drawing. An LED keeps a Steady, Slow, Fast or Heartbeat cue going while the state lasts.

properties.name: event
properties.title: Event
properties.description: When the output says it.

properties.name: output
properties.title: Output
properties.description: Which output says it: one of the saved Outputs of this kind (save a new one first).

properties.name: cue
properties.title: Cue
properties.description: What it says: an LED blinks (One, Two, Three), stays lit (Steady) or keeps a rhythm (Slow, Fast, Heartbeat). Test plays it on the saved output now.

properties.name: hapticFeedback
properties.title: Haptic Feedback
properties.description: What the haptic outputs say, and when: one row for each event and output. A motor is felt only while touching the device, so it answers the buttons: Press and Long Press once, when the button is let go; Held once a button has been held for a second (the cue that letting go is a long press). A press plays over Held.

properties.name: event
properties.title: Event
properties.description: When the output says it.

properties.name: output
properties.title: Output
properties.description: Which output says it: one of the saved Outputs of this kind (save a new one first).

properties.name: cue
properties.title: Cue
properties.description: What it says: the motor clicks the counts (One, Two, Three) or buzzes the rhythms (Steady, Slow, Fast, Heartbeat), once. Test plays it on the saved output now.

properties.name: audioFeedback
properties.title: Audio Feedback
properties.description: What the sound cards say, and when: one row for each event and output, with the events of GPIO Feedback. A sound card plays a state's cue once, when the state begins; a press plays over the others, Held comes before Problem, and Problem before Drawing.

properties.name: event
properties.title: Event
properties.description: When the output says it.

properties.name: output
properties.title: Output
properties.description: Which output says it: one of the saved Outputs of this kind (save a new one first).

properties.name: cue
properties.title: Cue
properties.description: What it says: a tone for each count (One, Two, Three) and rhythm (Steady, Slow, Fast, Heartbeat). Test plays it on the saved output now.

properties.name: quietFrom
properties.title: Quiet From
properties.description: The hour (0 to 23, the device's time) every output goes still, for the night; it wakes again at Quiet To. Either empty: never still. A Test still plays.

properties.name: quietTo
properties.title: Quiet To
properties.description: The hour (0 to 23) the outputs wake again after Quiet From: 22 to 7 is still from ten at night to seven in the morning.
